summary: AI agent identity management is the foundational security primitive for production agent deployments. The landscape spans Teleport's Agentic Identity Framework (four-layer model: identity, access, security, scheduling), Microsoft's Entra Agent ID + Agent Framework 1.0, Google Cloud Agent Identity (SPIFFE-based), APort (per-action authorization), SPIFFE/SPIRE (workload identity), and Red Hat's Kagenti on OpenShift. The consensus across all vendors and standards bodies (NIST, OWASP NHI Top 10, CISA) is that every agent must have a distinct, short-lived, cryptographically attested identity with policy-bound, just-in-time privileges and full audit trails at every action boundary.

key_trends: Every major vendor now treats agents as first-class identities with cryptographic attestation, not shared service accounts
SPIFFE/SPIRE has emerged as the de facto standard for workload-level agent identity across cloud, on-prem, and hybrid environments
The gap between 'identity' (who is this?) and 'authorization' (what can it do?) is being filled by policy engines at the action/tool-call boundary
Zero standing privilege, just-in-time token issuance, and ephemeral credentials are the consensus security posture
Delegation chains (agent acts on behalf of user/agent) require scope attenuation and cross-platform federation via OAuth 2.0 token exchange or A2A protocol
Regulatory pressure is mounting: NIST, OWASP, CISA, and EU AI Act all publishing agent-specific identity and governance frameworks in 2026
MCP (Model Context Protocol) has become the standard mediation point for identity verification and policy enforcement at tool boundaries
Hardened runtime isolation (Firecracker VMs, SPIFFE-based mTLS, WORM audit logs) is the production baseline for regulated deployments
competitor_gaps: No single vendor covers the full stack: SPIFFE handles infra identity but not authorization; APort handles per-action auth but not infra identity; Entra handles Azure-only identity
Multi-cloud/federated identity across heterogeneous agent frameworks remains an unsolved integration challenge
Standardized delegation chain audit (agent-1 → agent-2 → tool) with cryptographic proof is still nascent
Real-time policy enforcement at LLM inference time (not just tool call time) is only addressed by Teleport's LLM Proxy
Most solutions lack built-in human-in-the-loop approval gates for high-risk autonomous actions
recommended_angle: Position the guide as a practical reference for engineering and security teams deploying AI agents in production. Structure around the four-layer identity model (cryptographic identity → policy-bound access → runtime security → observability/governance), mapping each layer to concrete implementations from Teleport, Microsoft, Google, and open-source SPIFFE/SPIRE. Emphasize the 'identity-first, runtime-enforced' governance model and provide decision trees for choosing between vendor solutions based on deployment environment (cloud-native, hybrid, on-prem) and risk tier.
